name: Luigi Pulci
credit: Portrait of Luigi Pulci, detail of a fresco (traditionally identified; attributed to Filippino Lippi, Brancacci Chapel, Florence) · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Luigi Pulci (1432–1484) was born in Florence, the youngest of three poet brothers, and entered the household of the Medici as a favoured companion of Lorenzo the Magnificent, whose mother, Lucrezia Tornabuoni, urged him to write his great poem. He served the Medici on diplomatic errands and later as a captain in their service, and he died at Padua in 1484. Besides the epic he wrote a burlesque Beca da Dicomano, sonnets, and a series of letters to Lorenzo.

His masterpiece, the Morgante, tells in ottava rima of Charlemagne's paladins, of Orlando and the giant Morgante whom he converts, and of the treachery of Gano that leads to Roncesvalles. A first version in twenty-three cantari appeared about 1478; the enlarged text in twenty-eight, the Morgante maggiore, was printed at Florence in 1483. Comic, learned and irreverent by turns, it was a model for Boiardo and Ariosto, and Byron translated its first canto.
